text:
maddy: Heads-up — nightly-quant-smoke (h100) just flipped red on warmup. Seen on shard 7, failure looks like a kernel launch / invalid device function before OOM. cc @eng-ml-oncall :eyes:

eng-ci-bot: CI job failed: nightly/quant/l40/run-2026-03-16 (job id: 98572). Exit: 137. Summary: `kernel launch error: invalid device function` -> fallback to OOM spike in alloc path. Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/98572/logs

oliver: was there a driver or cuda image bump around that run?

maddy: yep — we rolled the canary driver last night from 531.68 -> 532.12 on the h100 pool. CUDA image stayed `redwood/quant:cuda12.2-rc3` (unchanged). Failure started immediately after the roll.

jess: which test exactly? small smoke or large model warmup?

maddy: warmup for quant_ggml_smoke.py — short sequence but alloc heavy. failing stack (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:11Z] libcuda: cuLaunchKernel() -> invalid device function
[2026-03-16T03:12:11Z] runtime: kernel launch failed, falling back to cpu path
[2026-03-16T03:12:12Z] alloc: tried 2GiB, got ENOMEM
```

raj: can you paste the `nvidia-smi -q` for that host and the container driver logs? wondering if the kernel modules match the userspace.

maddy: grabbed from the node: `Driver Version: 532.12`, `CUDA Version: 12.2`. Dmesg shows a few XID 31 before the crash.

oliver: XID31 usually mem access issue, but invalid device function suggests PTX/jit mismatch or a kernel compiled for different SM. Any PTX JIT messages in logs?

maddy: there is a PTX warning earlier: `ptx: ptx->sm_version mismatch for module weight_quant.cu` — could be from a recent PR that introduced a fused kernel. PR #4321 added a new quant kernel (fallback for L40).

jess: if it's PR+driver combo, we should bisect across commits and driver versions. quick ask: can someone rerun the job pinned to previous driver (531.68) and also run a bisect across commits?

eng-ci-bot: Suggested actions:
- Queue a rerun on the previous driver pool (canary revert).
- Start commit bisect job: nightly-bisect-quant (per-commit rebuild).

maddy: queued a targeted rerun on a node still on 531.68 (job 98573). Also queued nightly-bisect-quant starting from HEAD..~20 commits (job 98574).

ci-runner: rerun job 98573 started on node h100-node-07 (driver 531.68).

oliver: if rerun on 531.68 passes, that strongly points to driver interaction. if it fails there too, then likely the PR.

ci-runner: job 98573 logs: warmup passed, no kernel launch error. Test marked PASS.

maddy: good — so driver bump + new kernel seems to be the combo. bisect job 98574 is running, will post results.

raj: two immediate options: revert PR #4321 (quick rollback of kernel), or pin canary driver until we adapt kernel to 532.x. Recommend pin driver on canary for Dedicated pools and create an action to fix PTX compatibility.

jess: agree. also create a small repro docker that builds that new kernel and runs on both driver versions locally (helps validate before rolling drivers).

maddy: action items:
- pin canary driver back to 531.68 for rollout (oliver) :+1:
- revert PR #4321 on staging and create a follow-up to rework kernel for 532 (maddy) :memo:
- produce small repro image and test both driver versions (raj) :hammer_and_wrench:

oliver: I'll pin the driver on canary and add a note to the rollout plan. tagging @eng-ml-oncall for visibility.

eng-ml-oncall: acknowledged, will watch for follow-up.

maddy: bisect result (job 98574): narrowed to commit `d3b9a7f` which is the kernel change in PR #4321. reproducible on 532.12, passes on 531.68.

jess: great triage. leaving the revert up to release.

maddy: created revert PR #4330 and a follow-up issue describing PTX codegen assumptions and adding a CI job that runs new kernel builds against both drivers before merge.

oliver: thanks team. marking this resolved for now. will reopen if we see further flakes. :white_check_mark:

maddy: thx all :raised_hands:
